tests.title: A declined card explains what happened and keeps the cart
tests.description: An automatic run can check that an error appears, not that the wording helps a customer.
tests.preconditions: A cart with one item. The payment provider's test card that is always declined.
steps: Open the checkout and enter the declined test card
Read the message and look at the cart
tests.expected: The message says the card was declined and what to do next, in plain language. The cart still holds the item.

tests.title: The checkout is understandable with a screen reader and the focus order follows the visual order
tests.description: Needs a person with a screen reader: a script cannot judge whether the announcements make sense.
tests.preconditions: A cart with one item. VoiceOver (macOS) or NVDA (Windows) running.
steps: Open the checkout and move through it with Tab only
Listen to what the screen reader announces for each control
Compare the order of focus with the order on screen
tests.expected: Every control is announced with a name and role that match its label, and focus moves top to bottom, left to right.

tests.title: The checkout fits a phone and a tablet without sideways scrolling
steps: Open the checkout at 390×844 (iPhone 13) in portrait
Scroll through the whole page and use every control by touch
Repeat at the tablet breakpoint, 768 px wide
tests.expected: No content is cut off, there is no horizontal scrolling, and every control is large enough to tap.
